title: A smooth affine group and its marked residue torus descend to an integer model
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal, and $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $G\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with the multiplication, inverse and identity diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $r\geq0$ and let $i:\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]\hookrightarrow G_k$ be a closed subgroup immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], the Laurent spectrum having coordinatewise multiplication. There exist a subring $A_0\subset A$ generated by finitely many elements as a ring, a smooth affine group scheme $G_0$ of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, an isomorphism of $A$-group schemes $\alpha:G_0\times_{A_0}A\xrightarrow{\sim}G$, and a closed subgroup immersion $i_0:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]\hookrightarrow (G_0)_{\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)}$, where $\mathfrak p_0=A_0\cap\mathfrak p$, such that $\alpha_k\circ(i_0)_k=i$ under the canonical embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (objects, arrows, equalities); Tag 01ZP, lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation; Tag 0C0C, lemma-descend-smooth. Marked residue-field variant of the first reduction in Conrad Proposition 3.1.6, printed p.84.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ using its affineness. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $A\to B$ is smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-finite-type-model] to obtain a finitely generated subring $C_*\subset A$, a smooth $C_*$-algebra $B_*$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_{C_*}B_*\cong B$. Put $H_*=\operatorname{Spec}B_*$. The affine smoothness dictionary makes $H_*\to\operatorname{Spec}C_*$ smooth and of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] its base change $H_*\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C_*}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{C_*}B_*)$, with projections $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$; composing with $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the $A$-algebra isomorphism above (an isomorphism of $A$-algebras is one of tensor products by the pushout universal property) identifies it with $G$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. At this point this is an isomorphism of schemes, not yet of group schemes.

source.place: Tag 00TP, algebra.tex, lemma-finite-presentation-fs-Noetherian; affine translation of the initial model

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated subrings $C\subset A$ containing $C_*$. It is small and directed: adjoining the union of two finite sets of generators gives an upper bound. Its union is $A$, since any $a\in A$ lies in $C_*[a]$; any compatible family of ring maps on these subrings therefore extends uniquely to $A$. The transitions $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ are morphisms of affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the inverse limit of $\operatorname{Spec}C$. All stages are affine and hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Set $H_C=H_*\times_{C_*}C$. Each is affine and smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). They, their squares and cubes, and the base are of finite presentation: if $B_*=C_*[x]/(f)$, the $n$-fold product has coordinate algebra $C[x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(n)}]/(f(x^{(1)}),\ldots,f(x^{(n)}))$. The affine tensor identifications here, for $H_C$ and its fibre powers over $\operatorname{Spec}C$, are [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

source.place: Tags 01YW and 01ZM: directed integer subrings and the finite-presentation models

proof.text: Transport the given multiplication, inverse and identity of $G$ through the scheme isomorphism of step 1. Apply the morphism clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to each of the three maps, with source models $H_*^2,H_*,\operatorname{Spec}C_*$ and target model $H_*$. Each source and target is finitely presented by step 2, and the system has affine transitions and qcqs stages. There are stages carrying these three maps. Choose one common upper bound and pull the maps to it. Denote the resulting maps by $m_C:H_C^2\to H_C$, $v_C:H_C\to H_C$ and $e_C:\operatorname{Spec}C\to H_C$. Their base changes are the prescribed maps of $G$ under the fixed isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (2): multiplication, inverse and identity

proof.text: Over that stage form the associativity pair $m_C(m_C\times1),m_C(1\times m_C):H_C^3\to H_C$, the two unit pairs $m_C(e_C!,1),1$ and $m_C(1,e_C!),1:H_C\to H_C$, and the two inverse pairs $m_C(v_C,1),e_C!$ and $m_C(1,v_C),e_C!:H_C\to H_C$. Here $!$ is the structure map and paired maps are given by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. These five pairs agree after pullback to $A$, since they become the group axioms of $G$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. The equality clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out], applied to each pair and then to a common upper bound, makes all five equalities hold at a stage $C_1$. Consequently $H_{C_1}$ is a group scheme. The fixed scheme isomorphism after extension to $A$ respects its multiplication, inverse and identity by construction, hence is an isomorphism of group schemes. Smoothness was retained at every stage by step 2.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (3): the five group identities

proof.text: Restrict $I$ to the subrings containing $C_1$. Put $\mathfrak p_C=C\cap\mathfrak p$ and $k_C=\kappa(\mathfrak p_C)$. These are prime contractions. Explicitly $k_C=\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak p_C)$: by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $k_C=C_{\mathfrak p_C}/\mathfrak p_CC_{\mathfrak p_C}$, the local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ at $\mathfrak p_C$ modulo its maximal ideal, and there the fractions are $a/b$ with $b\notin\mathfrak p_C$. Thus inclusion of subrings induces the canonical injective maps $k_C\hookrightarrow k_{C'}\hookrightarrow k$. Every element of $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ has the form $\bar a/\bar b$ with $b\notin\mathfrak p$; adjoining $a,b$ to $C_1$ puts it in some $k_C$. Hence $k=\bigcup_C k_C$, with its ring-colimit universal property given by extending compatible maps on the union. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] the corresponding spectra have limit $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Their transitions are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and their stages qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

Over $k_{C_1}$ use the two fixed models $T_1=\operatorname{Spec}k_{C_1}[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ and $J_1=(H_{C_1})_{k_{C_1}}$. They are affine of finite presentation; for the torus use the presentation $k_{C_1}[t_1,u_1,\ldots,t_r,u_r]/(t_1u_1-1,\ldots,t_ru_r-1)$, and for $J_1$ substitute the coefficients of the finite presentation from step 2. Under the fixed identification $(J_1)_k\cong G_k$, the given map $i$ is a morphism $(T_1)_k\to(J_1)_k$. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) over the field system of step 5 to obtain a stage $C_2\supset C_1$ and a map $j_{C_2}:(T_1)_{k_{C_2}}\to(J_1)_{k_{C_2}}$ whose extension to $k$, followed by the fixed identification, is exactly $i$. No automorphism of the source torus is introduced.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (2): descend the specified parametrized residue-fibre map

proof.text: Both models in step 6 already carry their group structures: on the torus the operations are $t_a\mapsto t_a\otimes t_a$, $t_a\mapsto t_a^{-1}$ and $t_a\mapsto1$. Compare $j_{C_2}m_T$ with $m_H(j_{C_2}\times j_{C_2})$, $j_{C_2}v_T$ with $v_Hj_{C_2}$, and $j_{C_2}e_T$ with $e_H$. Their sources are respectively $T^2,T,\operatorname{Spec}k_{C_2}$, all of finite presentation, and their common targets are $J$. After extension to $k$ these are the homomorphism identities for $i$. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](3) to these three pairs and pass to a common upper bound $C_3$. They then hold over $k_{C_3}$, so the extended map $j_{C_3}$ is a group homomorphism in the diagrammatic sense of [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Tag 01ZM (3): multiplication, inverse and identity compatibility for the marked map

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] to $j_{C_3}$ over the field system indexed by $C\supset C_3$, whose transitions are affine as in step 5. Its limit map is $i$ under the fixed isomorphism, hence a closed immersion. All schemes and bases at the starting stage are affine, hence qcqs as in step 5. The starting map is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: its affine target coordinate ring maps to $k_{C_3}[t_a^{\pm1}]$, which is generated over that ring by the finitely many $t_a,t_a^{-1}$, since the structure maps preserve $k_{C_3}$. The cited descent result therefore gives $C_4\supset C_3$ where $j_{C_4}$ is a closed immersion. The homomorphism identities persist under pullback because composition and paired maps commute with pullback.

Take $A_0=C_4$, $\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak p_{C_4}$, $G_0=H_{C_4}$, $\alpha$ the fixed comparison with $G$, and $i_0=j_{C_4}$. The base ring is generated by finitely many elements by its membership in $I$. The group identities from step 4 persist under base change. The underlying affine scheme remains smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and finite presentation persists by the explicit base-changed presentation in step 2. Steps 7 and 8 make $i_0$ a closed subgroup immersion. At every field-stage transition the map was pulled back through the canonical inclusion $k_C\hookrightarrow k$; its extension, followed by $\alpha_k$, has remained the original $i$ from step 6. This is precisely $\alpha_k\circ(i_0)_k=i$. The construction also covers $r=0$: the Laurent presentation has no variables and all the same descent statements apply.
